basis: Developmental disability and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome. Broad genitourinary findings do not establish renal involvement; cardiac defects occur in 5-29%.
Most mesotheliomas arise in the pleura; peritoneal and other sites represent minority subtypes.
Defined by dermal melanocytosis and cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita, a cutaneous vascular malformation; common extracutaneous damage is not established.
Skin peeling, nail abnormalities and keratoses define the disorder; cheilitis is defining and oral leukoplakia occurs in 2/4 patients.
Degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons; muscle wasting and ventilatory failure result from denervation rather than primary muscle or lung disease.
Autoimmune bilateral granulomatous uveitis. Hearing impairment and cutaneous manifestations occur in only 5-29%.
Sterile eosinophilic inflammation of hair follicles is an immune-mediated cutaneous disorder; no common extracutaneous organ damage.
Intellectual disability, motor dysfunction, muscle wasting and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; distal amyotrophy occurs in 7/12.
Defined by hydrocephalus/posterior fossa malformations and a cutaneous capillary malformation. Eyelid nevus does not establish ocular damage.
Inherited motor neuron degeneration; muscle wasting and ventilatory failure reflect denervation rather than primary muscle or lung disease.
Maternal blocking autoantibodies cause transient thyroid hormone deficiency; associated symptoms do not establish lasting damage to other organs.
Hypomyelinating neurodegeneration; contractures and kyphoscoliosis each occur in 2/4, and gingival overgrowth in 2/4. Feeding difficulty alone adds no organ.
Meningioma arising within the cerebral hemispheres.
Inherited mitochondrial energy metabolism disorder affecting skeletal muscle; other organ manifestations vary across subtypes.
Congenital ventricular outflow malformation. Listed extracardiac syndromic anomalies are not intrinsic damage caused by DORV.
In situ epithelial carcinoma confined to the colon.
Molecular subtype of a central nervous system atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor; melanosomal gene expression does not indicate skin origin.
Ear canal atresia 80-99%; microphthalmia 30-79%. Nasal aplasia, oral clefts and gallbladder agenesis omitted by cap; cardiac/renal lesions less frequent.
Defined by infection; no single anatomical organ is affected in most patients across this umbrella.
Benign tumor of the sublingual salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Osteoporosis, joint hyperlaxity and congenital blindness characterize the syndrome; intellectual disability is reported without an established frequency.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in a bronchus or lung parenchyma.
Retinal ciliopathy and airway ciliary dyskinesia define the stated spectrum; cross-subtype frequencies are uncertain, so subtype-associated deafness is omitted.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with circulating malignant lymphocytes; hepatic involvement with hepatomegaly is reported in 30-79%. Spleen shares the haematologic axis.
Central autonomic control failure causes hypoventilation; respiratory failure does not establish lung disease. Constipation and episodic hypertension lack demonstrated organ damage.
